summary.text: Audrey Willis is the Democratic candidate for the Arkansas House of Representatives, District 35, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican Robert Thorne Jr. in a race with no incumbent.

A technology executive and co-founder of CodeCrew, she won the Democratic primary runoff on March 31, 2026, and says she is running on technology and workforce development, education and economic development.

paragraphs.text: Audrey Willis was born in Memphis, Tennessee, and graduated from Redan High School.
Her career experience includes co-founding CodeCrew, where she is chief innovation and programming officer, and serving as a mayoral appointee for Innovation and Performance Analysis.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she has worked to expand access to computer science education, workforce training and entrepreneurship opportunities across the Mid-South, serves on the boards of New Memphis and Epicenter Memphis, and is a member of the Delta Leadership Institute.
Willis advanced from a five-candidate Democratic primary on March 3, 2026, to a runoff, which she won over Joyce Gray, 60.9% to 39.1%.

She said her three key messages are technology and workforce development, youth and education, and economic development, and that she wants to represent West Memphis, Marion, Parkin, Earle and Turrell.
Among her stated priorities are expanding tech training, broadband access and apprenticeships, supporting teachers and STEM programs, and helping small businesses gain access to capital.
